Hello, I've followed the discussion but it's unclear if the problem has been resolved. I'd like to share my own experience with this error: I opened Device Manager, removed the serial port (COM1), re-scanned for hardware changes, and COM1 reappeared. After that, the IP address error disappeared and the controller connected successfully. I'm using Windows 7.

Hi, Here's how to find the correct COM port number for your converter: 1. Disconnect the converter from your PC. 2. Open Windows Device Manager and look under COM & LPT. 3. Connect your converter to the PC and note which COM port is added. The COM port added corresponds to your converter on that specific USB port. Note: Using a different USB port may result in a different COM port number. Select this COM port number in the software and try again. If it still doesn't work, the issue might be with the driver for your USB/RS232 converter. In my experience, many converters had compatibility problems. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges when trying to connect their [product_name] devices to PCs via COM ports, encountering unclear error messages such as "Unable to access the IP Address COM1." Differentiating between various device versions (such as [article_no] compared to newer versions) and properly setting up communication is complicated and not straightforward. There is confusion regarding device compatibility, network configuration, and device identification in the software, further complicated by ambiguous feedback from the system.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate smooth device recognition, straightforward instructions for connection setup, and helpful error messages while connecting their PC to [product_name] modules.
